problems.title: Count a regular polygon’s diagonals
problems.question: A regular n-gon has 252 diagonals. Find each interior angle.
problems.idea: Each vertex joins to n−3 nonadjacent vertices, and every diagonal is counted twice.
steps: Each interior angle is 180°−15°.

problems.title: Simplify a radical quotient carefully
problems.question: Simplify $\frac{x(x^2-a^2)^{-1/2}+1}{a(x-a)^{-1/2}+(x-a)^{1/2}}:\frac{a^2(x+a)^{1/2}}{x-(x^2-a^2)^{1/2}}+\frac1{x^2-ax}$.
steps: The original domain requires a≠0 and x>|a|. These ensure all roots and divisors are valid.
The first large fraction is [(x+d)/d]/(x/b)=(x+d)/(xc).
Dividing it by a²c/(x−d) gives (x²−d²)/(xa²c²)=1/[x(x+a)].
Add 1/[x(x−a)] to get [(x−a)+(x+a)]/[x(x²−a²)]=2/(x²−a²).

problems.title: Areas of polygons inside and outside one circle
problems.question: A regular dodecagon inscribed in a circle has area S. Find the area of the regular hexagon circumscribed about the same circle.
problems.idea: Divide each polygon into triangles from the centre.
formulas: Inscribed n-gon area=nR² sin(360°/n)/2; circumscribed n-gon area=nR² tan(180°/n).
steps: The dodecagon’s area is 12R² sin30°/2=3R²=S.
The outer hexagon’s area is 6R² tan30°=2√3R².
Substitute R²=S/3.

problems.title: The smallest term of a quadratic sequence
problems.question: Find the smallest term of aₙ=n²−17n−7 for positive integer n.
problems.idea: The vertex is halfway between n=8 and n=9.
steps: The nearest integers to 8.5 are 8 and 9. Both give square 0.25.
The minimum term is 0.25−79.25=−79.

problems.title: A telescoping lower bound
problems.question: Prove $1+1/2^2+\cdots+1/n^2>3n/(2n+1)$.
problems.idea: Compare each summand with a telescoping fraction.
steps: The comparison follows from 4k²−1≥3k². Equality holds only for k=1; it is strict for k≥2.
Sum the fractions. All interior terms cancel, leaving (3/2)(1−1/(2n+1))=3n/(2n+1).
For n≥2 at least one comparison is strict, proving the claimed strict inequality.
problems.answer: True for every integer n≥2; equality for n=1.
problems.note: As printed, the strict statement needs n≥2. It is false at n=1 because both sides equal 1.

problems.title: Domain and range of a fourth-root function
problems.question: Find the domain and range of $f(x)=\sqrt[4]{-x^2+x+2}$.
problems.idea: An even root requires a nonnegative radicand.
steps: Nonnegativity gives −1≤x≤2.
On this interval the radicand ranges continuously from 0 to 9/4.
Taking fourth roots gives the output interval [0,(9/4)^(1/4)].

problems.title: Solve two congruences
problems.question: Solve 3x+4≡0 (mod 14), 2x+1≡3 (mod 5) for integers x.
problems.idea: Reduce each congruence, then substitute one into the other.
steps: The first congruence gives x≡8 (mod14); the second gives x≡1 (mod5).
Write x=8+14k. Modulo 5, 3+4k≡1, so k≡2 (mod5).
Thus k=2+5t and x=36+70t.

problems.title: A quarter-circle with two internal semicircles
problems.question: A 90° sector has arc length 8π cm. Semicircles are built inside it on its two radii as diameters. Find the shaded part outside both semicircles.
problems.idea: The sum of the two semicircle areas equals the sector area, so the uncovered area equals their overlap.
formulas: Arc length=Rπ/2; lens area=2(quarter-circle area−right-triangle area).
steps: R=16, so each small semicircle has radius 8.
Their centres are distance 8√2 apart, and each half of the lens is a 90° circular segment.
The overlap is 2[(π·8²)/4−8²/2]=32π−64.
By inclusion-exclusion the shaded uncovered part has that same area.

problems.title: Two possible integer points of tangency
problems.question: The curves y=(a²/4)x²−2x+9 and y=ax meet at exactly one point with integer coordinates. Find that point.
problems.idea: For a≠0, set the discriminant of the intersection equation to zero.
steps: D=0 factors as (2−2a)(4a+2)=0, giving a=1 or a=−1/2.
The repeated root is x=2(a+2)/a². For a=1, (x,y)=(6,6). For a=−1/2, (x,y)=(12,−6).
When a=0, the curves are lines meeting at (9/2,0), which fails the integer-coordinate condition.
problems.note: Two different points satisfy the printed conditions. A restriction such as a>0 would be needed to select only (6,6).

problems.title: Area is largest for an equilateral triangle
problems.question: Prove that a triangle with semiperimeter p and area S satisfies p²≥3√3S.
problems.idea: Apply the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality to the three Heron factors.
steps: The three positive factors have product at most (p/3)³.
Hence S²≤p·(p/3)³=p⁴/27.
Taking nonnegative square roots gives S≤p²/(3√3). Equality requires p−a=p−b=p−c, so a=b=c.
problems.answer: p²≥3√3S, with equality exactly for equilateral triangles.
